Name: The creation of a residential parking permit system in certain Bronx community districts.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to the creation of a residential parking permit system in certain Bronx community districts

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure

Summary: This bill would require the Commissioner of Transportation to create a residential parking permit system in Bronx community districts 1, 2, 3, 9, and 10. Key features of this system include a prohibition on including streets where adjacent properties are zoned for commercial, office, or retail use; at least 20 percent of spaces in the permitted areas being available to non-residents of the relevant community district for short-term parking; the payment of fees to secure a permit; and an exemption for certain motor vehicles.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to the creation of a residential parking permit system in certain Bronx community districts

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Subchapter 2 of chapter 1 of title 19 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 19-175.11 to read as follows:
§ 19-175.11 Residential parking permit system in certain Bronx community districts. a. The commissioner shall create and implement a residential parking permit system in Bronx community districts 1, 2, 3, 9, and 10, which fixes and requires the payment of fees and the securing of a permit applicable to parking within the area in which such system is in effect in accordance with the provisions of this section.
b. In creating the residential parking permit system required under subdivision a of this section, the commissioner shall:
1. Designate the specific areas in which such system applies, provided that the commissioner shall not designate any street where the adjacent properties are zoned for commercial, office, or retail use;
2. Provide the times of the day and days of the week during which permit requirements shall be in effect; 
3. Make not less than 20 percent of all spaces within the permitted areas available to non-residents of the relevant community district and provide for short-term parking of not less than 90 minutes in duration in such areas; 
4. Provide that motor vehicles registered pursuant to section 404-a of the vehicle and traffic law be exempt from any permit requirement; 
5. Provide the schedule of fees to be paid for permits; and 
6. Provide that such fees shall be credited to the general fund of the city.
§ 2. This local law takes effect 120 days after it becomes law.
